entries.speaker: D
entries.text: House sold! We went to the Morgan’s to stay the night, they had a new puppy - Troubadour - he was teething, so he chewed a lot. Pizza and sausages for dinner - ice cream after, made a fruit salad with watermelon in it, difficult to get out pips!

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Car broke down twice, oh dear! We were late to have our last cholera injections.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: SET OFF Mileage = 27600 - going to Luxfords

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Rhiannon’s Birthday. I slept on the floor, my injection arm hurt and I felt very tired when I woke up. Watched television and played with rabbits, 8 new baby ones, 4 weeks old, very nice. Went swimming but no-one would come in with me. Had lunch, fish and chips, I had an egg. Had the fruit salad and ice cream as well. Played, Olympic Games, but Rhiannon fell over and everyone disagreed with each other … Went to Cobham with Mum to buy some cassettes, but car broke down, bought 3 empty cassettes, took car to garage, bought some sweets. Went back to Morgan’s, got F & H and are now driving to Luxfords. Dad is taking a train. Arrive at Lux, have dinner, bed.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: At Luxford’s, sleeping in caravan, baby Anabelle staying the night.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: At Luxford’s, lunch, with Betty, Mary, husband and children staying, went swimming.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 27689 (89 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Slept in caravan again. Dad went to work in London (in his old suit!) Stayed the morning at Betty’s, swam, slept and read. Lunch with Betty, pizza and C.M. pie, fruit salad after. Went for another short swim, then drove to Dover, fetched Dad, (all trains went wrong). Waited in queue, and then got on Ferry. Found place to sit and then, off Dad’s jacket! (It was old and worn out) got some very queer looks from other people! Used up all English money buying food and drink, revolting but fun. Arrived in France and drove, we were very tired, finally stopped and slept in Fred.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: Going on ferry to Calais, ripped up Dad’s jacket [and flung it overboard to signify the end of working in England]. Then we had dinner at 11 o’clock.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Cross Belgium border. Mileage = 27828 (228 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Outside Aachen. Mileage = 27977 (377 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Slept next to Main River at Aachen. V. pleasant. Many big barges.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Camping Wien Sud (Vienna) (near Schonbrun Palace).

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Past Nurmburg Mileage = 28284 (684 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Got to Munich about 3.30pm. Went to Deutsche Museum. Excellent. Beer etc at Hofbrauhaus - kids amazed. Telephoned Nahas. Went to Langweider Zee campsite. Noisy, crowded but good hot water.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Went round Munich.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: At night, we went to the Beerhall, there were lots of people there, bandsmen and barmaids were dressed in national costume. We had three plates, all of them had some kind of sausage, Dad had a big 1/2L / 1pt glass of beer, we had lemonade.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: I have seen an armoured car, a jet and these trucks. Two troop carriers.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Camping at Zadar - Ponta Bajilo(??) Went to Europ Market. Went to Nahas. Had a snack. Took D to Dr Mercimer(?), 63 Leopold Strasse, cost 44.80DM - ear infection, take Penicilin and Aspirin. No swimming!

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 28417 (817 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Stayed last night at campsite, had showers etc. then drove into Munich and went to see Nahas they were very interesting. Mum asked Johan about a Doctor seeing my ear, we did some research, went down to a chemist’s and found that we would have to see a Doc at 3.30. We went back and talked to Dagmar some more, had lunch, went for a walk, went to Doc’s. I had some pills. Left, and drove to Austria.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Into Yugoslavia. Villach Pass v. steep - 18% in places. Mileage = 28668 (1068 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Found a place in a little forest to sleep, wet, but nice. In morning, made houses for Paddington, and took thing out of my ear, can’t swim for 3 / 4 days, drove into Salzburg to see old city, but couldn’t really find it. We walked round, window shopping, and looking around until we came to a little square with a beautiful fountain with seahorses. We went to a nice cafe and had some delicious hot chocolate with cream.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We are now driving to Yugoslavia, wonderful scenery. Entered YS and found campsite, at long last. Very crowded, not very nice.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: Went to Salzburg. I saw a nice fountain there. Found 65 pfennings and bought some soldiers, then we went to a horrible camp site. On the way to it we went through a big tunnel and up a steep hill. Fred only just made it.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We have been to Salzburg. There were lots of lovely things in the shops. I went to a restaurant. I had Apple Soft. Francis had Coke. Mummy and Denise had hot chocolate. Daddy had beer.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Camped 12 kms outside Senj near watermill into little bay. Idyllic surrounds. Foul loos!

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Postojna. Got up and went to caves, they were beautiful, long queue, bought tickets and got on a little train, it was cold in the caves. We went along on the train and then had to get off and walk round with an English speaking guide, who told us about the various caves as we went through. There were lots of stalagmites, and tites, they were very beautiful. Got on train again and went out.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: In the Postojna Jama in Yugoslavia. We got onto an electric train. It took us to the caves. Then the train stopped and we got out. From there on we had a guided tour. Went to some large caves, there were lots of stalagmites and stalactites.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: I stayed in a campsite by the sea. And went to see some beautiful caves and there were lots of halls. I went on a train too. Spaghetti hall - stalactites looked like spaghetti. And we had an ice cream. I stroked some sea urchins by the sea and I swam in cold water.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Stayed in camp.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We are at a campsite by the seaside - it’s quite nice, revolting loos, but nice fresh water. I went swimming, very carefully, so as not to get my ears wet, very cold. Went for a walk and reached some warmer water, lovely to swim in.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: Found lots of sea urchins and stroked some. Helena found a dried spider starfish. This was in a campsite in Yugoslavia.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 28851 (1250 miles travelled). Saw lots of accidents - held up for 2 hours by one.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 28923 (1323 miles travelled). Stayed night at VERY nice camp a few miles past Omis(?) in a pine forest going down to stony beach. There was a full moon so we walked by beach in the moonlight. VERY pleasant.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Got up early and got the van ready. Mum and Dad went back to Senj to get petrol and bread. Went to swim, it was cold, so we couldn’t pluck up the courage to swim, we found a little rock pool, and then a starfish, we put the starfish in the pool, it was a pretty one, then Mum and Dad came back with some delicious bread. We all got in the van and started the drive to Dubrovnik, eating the warm bread and biscuits, we have come upon a crash, because the road is very wet, no one can get through, so we will probably be here for a few hours. At last, we finally moved on, but passed about 10 more accidents, it was so late that we didn’t go to Dubrovnik, we stopped at a lovely campsite, and went swimming in warm blue water.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: On the way to Dubrovnik, we saw a crash. A lorry had smashed into a caravan. The road was wet and the lorry skidded into the caravan after doing a three quarters turn. The Police came, we had lunch then me and Helena and Denise went to pick blackberries. The people pulled the lorry. It did not move. They moved the caravan. Some traffic could have got through but he was trying to move the lorry. At last a bus tried to go through.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went to a nice campsite. We parked Fred in some trees. Helena, Denise and I had a swim, it was lovely. Then we went to the van and had dinner. After that Mum and Dad came, I kindled a fire by myself. There was a path on the water made by the moon.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: On the way to Dubrovnik, a lorry had a crash. It was interesting but we had to wait a long time.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 29083 (1483 miles travelled). Had a walk to shop to buy breakfast etc. Lovely crusty bread - 120 Dinars. Drove off at 11am towards Dubrovnik. Sunny.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 29191 (1591 miles travelled). Went to Juloshina(?) Line to book in ?? ??

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Had another lovely swim in the sea, it was a lovely pebble beach. Before swimming we walked up to a shop to get some breakfast. Then Mum and Dad came swimming with us. Then we left and went on driving to Dubrovnik. When we finally arrived we went to a nice pebble beach, but we had to pay! We had a lovely swim there, we went to a nice market and bought some fruit and veg. After that we went to the old city, it was very beautiful. Some of the streets were very narrow though. When we went up onto the city walls, we saw some men playing bowls. Then it was late, so we went to a campsite, it’s enormous! We played poker and drank whiskey and coke at 12.00 midnight.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went to a huge castle. Some people were playing bowls. We went outside of the walls. The sea was terrifying when we were inside, Helena tried on some shoes but we did not get her any, but we did get some smoked ham.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: Went to see a lovely castle. Bought smoked bacon. Went to harbour and market. Bought ice cream. I had a lovely swim and played pebbles. It was fun.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Still on big campsite, loos etc. revolting, just lazing around, had lunch and then left for Dubrovnik. Found the nice beach and went swimming again, lovely. When we came back up to the car, we got changed into warm clothes, for the ferry. We then went back to the little market and then on to the ferry port, we had to wait a long time to get on though. At last, we are on and the ferry has left the port, we’ve had dinner, and are playing a few games before we go to bed. Helena and I squashed into the same sleeping bag, but we swapped and changed before we really settled down.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went to a beach where we swam. It was a pebble beach. There were lots of waves. I had a cold shower. After a long wait we got on the ferry to Dubrovnik. We had dinner and tried to go to sleep. I was sharing with the girls. In the end, Mum said that we could get up and go with Dad. He had three German friends, they taught me and Denise poker. At ten I had to go to bed.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: I woke up late and went to a pebble beach then we went to the big boat and slept on deck. It was cold, dry and windy. The moon was full.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: The ferry at last arrived in Corfu and after a bit of fuss, we got off, then we drove round to Gouvia Bay, and found Alegra, Nono came out in the dinghy to fetch us and then we all swam. We carried [on] swimming, eating and lazing around at appropriate times until bed time, it was good to sleep in a nice bed again.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We are in Gouvia Bay with some other yachts, the water is lovely and warm, and the sea gets a deeper blue, the deeper the water gets.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: In the morning, I woke up, got dressed and had breakfast of chocolate and bread. We got off the ferry. We almost had to go to Iguamenitsa. After we had got off the ferry we parked near a hotel. We had trouble finding Nono. At last we got on Alegra, it was lovely. We swam. There were three JB 007 books I started - The man with the Golden Gun. For dinner we had ham and salad then we went to bed.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: Corfoo (sic) We have arrived at Corfoo. Nono has taken us aboard Allegra. I go and get into my bathing suit. I can swim but not very well. Nono has fixed a rope to the side of Allegra. I can nearly float. I’ve also learnt to do breaststroke, frog leg and to tread water. Nonno has a grey motor dinghy which we pretend is a six eyed shark. Denise sleeps in the front cabin. I sleep with Mummy and Daddy in the back cabin.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: This morning we went out shopping in Corfu, apart from food, we were shopping mainly for sandals. We did at last get some, and on the way back to the cafe where we were meeting Nono, I bought a Beatles cassette, 1962-1966. At the little cafe we had ice cream and baclava, it was absolutely delicious! When we got back we swam and had lunch in the van. I listened to the Beatles, they were good.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We bought an inflatable dinghy and at 12.00 (midnight) we went swimming by light of moon, saw some phosphorescence, cold, only Dad and I swam.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: 12.39 We went swimming. Denise saw some pholsurphrent (sic).

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: In the morning, we went shopping. We got lots of shoes. Denise got a Beatles Cassette 1962-1966. On the way back, I got some H0-00 scale soldiers.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: When we got back, me and Helena caught crabs. We got two - one about this big (pic) and 5 hermit crabs.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: I slept in the foc’sle - it was lovely. There is a little toilet and basin and a beautiful bed and two portholes. We have bought a dinghy.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: This morning, straight after breakfast, Nono started the engine and we chugged out of Gouvia Bay, and went to Corfu port, we shopped around a bit, and then set off again. We arrived in a nice little bay and had lunch at a restaurant. We also had dinner at the little restaurant with Joana and David, they were very nice.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: When Alegra started moving, my soldiers moved as though they were alive. There was a column and they went into small groups. We had lunch with Joanne on a terrace. In the bay we made an aquarium - it had 4 starfish, one with nine tentacles, 3 were black and one was orange and black and purple. There were lots of sea urchins, some black, some red, some purple, some brown, some a mixture of colours. Also there was a crab the same size as the ones I caught yesterday.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: I have made an aquarium. In it there are two small spider starfish and one big one and a nine legged one and some sea urchins. I also went to see a girl called Joanna and had chips and omelette and salad. We saw a wreck.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We slept the night in the little bay, in the morning, we went back to another bay, where we had lunch with some nice people, the man had a catamaran, we all went to the beach to look at it and swim then we went back to Gouvia.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Stayed in bed quite late, we were going by the time I got up. By the time we’d finished breakfast, we were just entering Corfu harbour and when we’d arrived we went on shore, it was very difficult getting on and off the boat, we had to get onto the boat next to us, and then jump quite a long way! When we came back, the new water pump was being fitted. We then set off again and were underway quite a while. We arrived in a little bay surrounded by hills, and other bays. It was very beautiful. We went and played out on the beaches, making aquariums etc then we went to a little village and ate out.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: The Bay. This Bay was in the Mediterranean Sea in Greece. The end of it is blocked by a spit. The land was sandy with trees. There are sea urchins dotted around the shore. The bottom was weed with patches of sand. The land was mainly gorse, olive and pine.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Still in little bay, just lazing about. Afternoon, go for a little walk, we went over in the dinghy, after pulling it up on the beach, we walked up to a wide path and proceeded along it. It led, for some time, along the coast, quite high up, we could see the beautiful colours of the water and there were lots of wild herbs along the path. Soon the path went further inland, and there was some dispute as to which path to follow, we chose the one that carried on up, through some small trees, eventually there was a choice of paths again, we saw what looked like some ruins and made for them. It was in fact an old house, it was very big. On the way back we almost lost the path.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: Nature on the Island. The main things on the island were Cyprus trees. Also there were huge groves of olive trees. I saw lots of webs; most of them Funnel-webs. (Pic)

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: Picture of ‘Different Trees’

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We are still in little bay, but hope to go to Paxos at around 4.30 this afternoon. Nono is working on the water pump, so the rest of us are setting off in the dinghy to look at some caves. We are going out to a small island, there are quite a few caves in its cliffs. The first few are really just niches, but then we came to a bigger one - carefully we took the boat in, it was quite frightening, we went on to see some others but they weren’t quite as good. We went to Paxos, the sea was quite calm but I felt a little ill, had a rather disastrous evening out, but Nono bought me a ring.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: (Pic)

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We have been to Newton’s Cove. The water was see-through and blue. There was light blue where there was sand and a colour like this *(dark green) when there was weed. One night we went to dinner at a restaurant on the mainland. Francis and I went and stroked a donkey. Soon we saw a man leading a white goat on a leash with a bell round it’s neck. Three black goats followed. It got dark quite quickly, and when we were going back I walked into a barbed wire fence.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: This is a bit like the ring Nonno bought for me, in fact, the shopkeeper was Nonno’s friend and after choosing a ring out of a bowl, he said we could have it free. Nonno also bought Mum a jumper.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: This is a bit like the shawl I bought but I used a thick felt-tip so it does not look very good.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We went for a walk along the coast and saw lots of interesting bits of beach. The Island had made lots of progression. It was not as nice as it had been, very crowded.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: Berries on the island. (Pic). The cypress very is a big berry - it is about (pic) that big. It is cracked and wrinkled. I threw them at DD. The berry bush is a bush with small red berries - about twice the size of a pinhead. They were very smooth and round. Olives are the main product of Corfu. They are grown in huge orchards or groves. They press them into olive oil

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We had lots of rain at night, and in the morning, my bedroom, which is the foc’sle, leaked, a lot, not a pleasant surprise in the early morning! At the moment, I am sitting under a sky full of clouds, it’s early evening and the clouds are lots of different colours. Some are fleecy and soft but are tinged with very light bluey-grey or creamy-yellow these are all soft and sort of three dimensional, but there are also much darker clouds in shapes I can’t describe, mostly like this: (small drawing here). Some of them the sun have given lovely, lighter sides to, but some of the smaller clouds are drifting away. The whole lot is shakily reflected in the sea, it is very beautiful, added to the already blue sea.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: Gouvia is about 4 times as big as Milbourne lodge [where Francis went to school in England]. There are 32 boats and Alegra, ten had dinghies. The water was about …

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: Gouvia Bay. These are some of the trees. (pic)

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Off Allegra. Drove to Paleokastrizza. Visit to cave, swim, lunch. Drove to Glyfada Beach - long, sandy with lily? white flowers. Lovely smelling, poking out of the brownish sand. On to Aguis Giordis. Stopped en route in olive grove. Invited for glass of wine by Tom & Helen Wrightson of York. Just building a house. V. pleasant.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Today we left the boat, and went in the van, to the other side of Corfu, we followed almost exactly the route we took 3 years ago on motor scooters, then we came to a beach with a big cave which we swam to. We camped in a nice olive grove, and some people invited us to have drinks, we had a pleasant and interesting conversation.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: Went to Paleoskatritsa - a beach in Corfu. We swam to a small cave - it was super. I dived off a rock. There were lots of people. Me and Helena made a H0-00 scale castle. I filled it with Foreign Legion [mini-soldiers]. Then we went to Glyfada.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: Went to a beach, swam to a nice cave, had lunch and built a castle. Then we walked home.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 29303 outside Gouvia (1703 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Us children walked down to a beach in the morning, it was a long way but worth it when we got there. We tried surfing on the waves, it was very fun. Then we went to tea at the Broadbents(?), they are very, very nice. We had a shower and washed our hair there as well. Had takeaway chicken and chips for dinner.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: Then me and the girls walked to Agrogeordis. It was a huge sandy beach. We surfed in phantom. Then we went to Sebastian’s house. We played with Argo. By mistake, Sebastian threw the ball over the house.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: I have built a sand castle and it was quite big with thick walls. Sabrina and I made a treehouse and played with Paddington. (‘Not very good.’ Mum)

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Ferry to Igoumenitsa.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 29381 (1781 miles travelled). Camped on main ?? near Heisovan?. Lots of goats. Some of the land is open. Fertile plateau. Took some photos of mules, mule ?? and goats.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Today is our last day in Corfu. We are actually in Corfu town now, and have been in a nice park. Mum and Dad came and we all sat on a little wall doing our diaries and eating nougat. Then we drove onto the Ferry. When we arrived, we drove through the rain, up to some mountains, we drove up and down, and around the mountains, in and out of the clouds, they were very low and misty (the clouds). We saw lots of herds of sheep and goats, crossing the road, or grazing on the mountains, always with a shepherd or shepherdess and sometimes, a dog, we also saw some long lines of mules, horses and donkey, carrying firewood and other things.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: It is our last day in Corfu. We are catching the one o’clock ferry to Igoumenitsa. The ferry is a converted tank landing craft. I found out that the vehicle can float with its door down and the anchor is bigger than Dad. From Igoumenitsa we went through some mountains. We saw mule trains carrying wood and some single mules. We drove through some clouds. There are lots of sheep and goats. We turned off the road for the night. There was a stream with lots of tadpoles and frogs, a very few about 2 inches long, they were camouflaged on top and yellow and blue underneath.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We have been in another car ferry from Corfu to a place in Greece. We are driving up a mountain in the evening. We stopped at a valley with a stream and some frogs. I made a bivouac by a tree. We saw lots of mules, sheep and goats. The goats came quite closer and so did a few mules. The sheep were on the next mountain.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Rained buckets during night, v. cold and windy. Little stream with tadpoles, frogs, yellow and splodged underneath.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 29455 (1855 miles travelled). Photo of stork on church. Meteora caves v. good. Finished film. Started new one with telephoto.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 29539 (1939 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 29615 Thessoloniki (2015 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We camped last night just off the road, in the mountains. There were a few trees dotted around and a little stream. In the stream there were big and small tadpoles and frogs, the big frogs had spotty yellow tummies. There were also some small nests. We were slightly on a slant, and it was very cold. Lots of animals went past us, sheep and goats and a small mule train, nearly all the animals had bells round their necks, they made a pleasant, assorted, jingling sound. When we drove down out of the mist, it warmed up, we went to see some monasteries on top of some enormous rocks, we also climbed on to see a cave.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: It has been raining today. We had porridge. Helena and I tracked the stream. We found it ended in marsh then we found some more stream. It had no life in so we transported some life then we had to go. We drove to some monasteries! They were on some huge steep rocks like towers. We tried to go into one but you had to pay and there were huge queues. There were lots of blackberries, we picked some. Then we tried to go to some old caves probably used by hermits. The path was very narrow.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We have driven to some monasteries. They were nice. Daddy and Denise wanted to go inside but they could not. The monasteries were on some steep rock mountains. We tried to climb to a cave but we could not.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Camped well past Thessoloniki after miles of dreary road through plains.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 29746 (2146 miles travelled). Seen lots of tobacco leaves. Camped outside Xanthis near fields growing maize and pumpkins for seeds.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Today we drove a lot, first on good roads, but then we turned off on to, as the map called it, a ‘non-asphalt’ road, the surface was very bad, and it wound round and round the mountains, We finally reached the small village of Olympus, shopped and swam. Then we drove about a mile out and stopped for lunch by the sea, we thought we were secluded, and pranced about naked, only to discover that we were just next to the ground of a big Hotel! We drove on, and in a wood mum spotted a tortoise on the road, we stopped and played with it.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: Sent postcard to Adam Hill. Dear Adam, I have been in a tank-landing craft. It has an anchor as big as a man. I also went to some caves, they were huge. One had a bridge made by Ruskie POWS in the First war. Love from Francis.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went along a very long road. There was a tortoise, I tried to feed it. We had chocolate and bread. It was nice chocolate, it tasted peppermintish. For lunch we stopped at Olympus Beach. I found a wasps nest. I lifted up a stone, the end was covered with wasps. I swam twice on a lagoon, I saw a six inch dragonfly (?).

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We woke up by a stream that was in a ravine. I saw a birds nest. Francis and I went to pick some flowers. We crushed and mixed them and put them in the nest. Later on we found a tortoise. He was on a road that ran through an oakwood. It was eleven o’clock and we played with him but he would not eat his elevenses which was a dandelion leaf.
